data.exact_reserve_text: During 2014 the Syndicate released GBP 77.4m of technical reserves in respect of prior periods, arising predominantly from the Marine, Property and Treaty Divisions (2013: GBP 79.4m, primarily from the Energy and Treaty Divisions). These releases were due to favourable claims development on losses in 2014.

named_events.loss_description: notably the tragic loss of over 300 lives on the Sewol ferry in Korea, and a number of charterer liability losses, which we continue to monitor closely.
only pausing after the second Malaysian Airline loss in July as the market attempted to recover some of the losses of the last 12 months.

further deterioration in the Costa Concordia loss, although this remained comfortably within our reinsurance programme. The removal of the Costa Concordia wreck has now been successfully completed and the vessel moved to a breakers yard in Genoa.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2014 was GBP 1,332.5m. During 2014 the syndicate reported gross releases on prior years of GBP 77.4m, driven predominantly by favourable claims development in the Marine, Property and Treaty divisions. The release is described as arising from positive development on losses in 2014; no gross per-line quantified breakdown of the release is provided.

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Balance Sheet (Claims outstanding, liabilities) 2013 comparative column = GBP 1,332.5m (page 17). Prior year movement is taken from Note 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' which states a release of GBP 77.4m (page 22) and is taken as a gross figure. The release is allocated 'predominantly' to Marine, Property and Treaty divisions but no per-line gross amounts are provided. Named events listed in the report are mentioned without quantified net/gross losses to the syndicate. No gross claims development triangle was found in the notes. Accident and health gross premium appears as a small negative (-0.1) in the segmental table.
